{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Base Terms)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement (document excerpt reviewed: 3.1 Term and Base Terms) 
**Status:** 18 findings verified — 3 critical, 5 high, 9 medium, 1 low

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review. The commercial architecture is workable, but the risk allocation is materially one-sided in IBM's favour in three areas that we regard as must-fix before signature:

- **Liability (§ 9.1).** The cap is mutual at 12 months' charges, but the floor is $100,000 (against our $1,000,000 preferred position), is measured on charges *paid* only, there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and § 9.1(2) **wholly excludes IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data** — which guts our remedy in a hosting deal.
- **Indemnities (§ 8.1 / § 8.2).** IBM's indemnity is IP-only (meeting our fallback for IP), with no cover for IBM's breach of law, IBM-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data, or IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Meanwhile our reverse indemnity at § 8.2(a)(3) covers any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — effectively a one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services. This is a walk-away item.
- **IP ownership (§ 7 / § 5.4).** All delivered Materials default to Type II (IBM-owned), giving us only an internal-Enterprise licence with no right to modify, and nothing in the Agreement confirms we retain rights in our Content and Customer Components.

Beyond these, our exit economics are unquantified: convenience termination under § 3.4 is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges with no ceiling and no refund of prepaid charges, there is **no transition assistance, data return or deletion obligation anywhere** in the Agreement, and there is **no vendor insurance provision at all** despite IBM operating the hosting environment and processing personal information. Warranty protection is thin (reasonable care and skill only, with Materials supplied "AS IS" under § 5.4(c)).

On the positive side, four playbook risks are simply absent and we should preserve that: no exclusivity or non-compete on us (§ 14.16 Freedom of Action expressly preserves both parties' freedom to contract with others), no MFN burden, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment (§ 4.1), no audit right against us, and no non-solicitation restriction on us (§ 14.8). Governing law is already New York, our preferred choice; only the forum element is missing.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue in brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | IBM indemnity is IP-only; missing breach of law, IBM-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct heads. Our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity for any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is far broader than the playbook allows. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers (with § 7) | Materials default to Type II (IBM-owned), internal-Enterprise licence only, no modification right; no confirmation that we retain rights in Content and Customer Components. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Floor $100,000 on charges "paid" only; no Excluded Claims carve-outs; § 9.1(2) excludes all IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 14.10 Assignment | Restricts only our assignment; M&A carve-out omits affiliates and asset sales and is unclear on consent; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a competitor. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Uncapped early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A / Service Option Attachments, with no stated ceiling; § 10 also preserves IBM's claim for Services that would have been rendered but for our breach. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 12.1 License | Grant is expressly "revocable" with no standard and runs to Customer only — Affiliates and contractors operating the Services for us are not covered (§ 14.17 grants nothing further). |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Compliant** | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No sole-supply or exclusive-dealing obligation on us; § 14.16 confirms each party may contract with others. No redline. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Compliant** | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant on us; only restrictions are the § 14.11 resale bar and licence-scope limits. No redline. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law is our preferred position, but there is no venue or forum clause and no arbitration provision; exclusive New York County jurisdiction is missing. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 3.2 Renewal | Auto-renews for a term equal to the prior term (so multi-year renewals where an Order Form sets a multi-year initial term) on 90 days' non-renewal notice; renewal uplift uncapped. |
| 11 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | We have a ~30-day convenience right and IBM has none (good), but the right is conditioned on open-ended early termination charges and there is no refund of prepaid charges (§ 3.5 only accelerates our payment obligations). |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | No transition assistance, Content return/export or deletion-certification obligation anywhere; § 3.5 addresses only our payment obligations. All our data sits in IBM's hosting environment. |
| 13 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Reasonable care and skill only; no conformance-to-documentation or malicious code warranty and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy. § 5.4(c) supplies all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (verification: fail) | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | No usage, metering or licence-compliance audit right exists against us; § 11.3 is an abuse/acceptable-use investigation right. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is an artefact of there being no audit clause to parameterise. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | **Compliant** | § 4.1 Charges | No terms- or pricing-parity obligation on us. Absence of a vendor-granted MFN in our favour is a commercial upside item, not a playbook deviation. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Compliant** | § 4.1 Charges | No minimum, committed volume, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic; charges apply only to Services ordered. § 11.5 Capacity Planning imposes no usage floor or cap. |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification: fail) | § 14.8 Personnel | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on us; § 14.8 covers only each party's own personnel and IBM's subcontracting. Failed duration and general-solicitation sub-checks are non-probative because there is no restriction to parameterise. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.12 Risk of Loss | Agreement is silent on insurance, yet IBM operates the hosting environment, holds Customer Components (§ 14.12) and processes personal information on our behalf (§ 14.18). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions we should not sign as drafted:

1. **§ 8.2(a)(3) — one-way Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services.** Indemnifying IBM against any Services Recipient claim "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" is expressly a walk-away item under the playbook, only partly mitigated by the relief in § 8.2(c). We require this narrowed to our breach of law or of this Agreement.
2. **§ 9.1(2) — blanket exclusion of IBM liability for loss of or damage to our records or data.** In a hosting deal this removes our principal remedy and must be deleted; it also needs to be read with the absence of any data-breach indemnity in § 8.1.
3. **§ 5.4(c) — all Materials "AS IS" with no carve-out.** Combined with the absence of any conformance, malicious code or remedy provision, this sits close to the walk-away position on warranties. At minimum the § 5.1 warranties must be carved out of the disclaimer.
4. **No vendor insurance where IBM processes personal data.** The playbook treats a vendor processing personal data with no insurance as a walk-away; we require the covenant at § 14.12A.
5. **§ 3.2 — automatic multi-year renewals.** Where an Order Form specifies a multi-year initial term, § 3.2 produces automatic multi-year renewals, which is at the walk-away boundary. Renewal terms must be fixed at 12 months.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Redlines issued (critical and high):**
1. § 8.1 — add IBM indemnity heads for breach of applicable law, IBM-caused unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, placed inside § 8.1 so they benefit from the uncapped treatment in § 9.1(a) and the existing notice/control/cooperation procedure; narrow our § 8.2(a)(3) indemnity to our breach of law or of this Agreement.
2. § 9.1 — raise the mutual floor to $1,000,000 on fees **paid or payable**, add a mutual Excluded Claims provision (confidentiality/data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and delete the § 9.1(2) data-loss exclusion. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion in § 10, with its carve-out for our payment obligations, is acceptable as drafted.
3. § 7 / § 5.4 — flip the default to Type I (Customer-owned), extend the Type II licence to modification and use for our business, and add an express Customer ownership / no-joint-ownership statement for Content and Customer Components.
4. § 14.10 — add an affiliate and substantially-all-assets carve-out for our assignment without IBM consent, plus a reciprocal reasonableness-qualified consent requirement on IBM with a competitor prohibition. **Fallback offered:** mutual successor assignment on notice. No change to § 3.3, which is breach-only.
5. § 3.4 — delete the uncapped early termination charge and add a 30-day pro-rata refund of prepaid charges. **Fallback offered:** cap the charge at three months' recurring charges as the sole amount due on convenience termination.
6. § 12.1 — extend the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and contractors operating the Services on our behalf, and tie revocation to expiration or termination under § 3 rather than IBM's discretion.

**Redlines issued (medium and low):**
7. § 14.3 — append exclusive New York County (state and federal) venue, leaving the choice-of-law sentence intact.
8. § 3.2 — fix renewal terms at 12 months, shorten our non-renewal notice to 30 days, add a 60-day IBM renewal reminder, and cap uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
9. § 3.5 — insert the playbook transition assistance and Content return/export and deletion-certification obligations (§ 3.5 already survives termination under § 14.2, so no survival amendment is needed).
10. § 5.1 / § 5.4(c) — add a 90-day conformance warranty, a no-malicious-code warranty and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and carve the § 5.1 warranties out of the "AS IS" disclaimer.
11. New § 14.12A — vendor insurance covenant at preferred levels (CGL $1M/$2M, E&O $2M, cyber $5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request). **Fallback offered:** E&O $1M / cyber $2M.

**No action required (preserve current drafting):** EXCLUSIVITY, NONCOMPETE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, AUDIT and NOSOLICIT. We are not proposing edits on the two "needs review" items — inserting audit or non-solicit machinery would require first drafting a restriction against ourselves, which is worse than the status quo.

**Diligence to complete before signature:**
- **Attachment A, the Service Option Attachments and each Order Form are not part of the reviewed text.** We must review them for (i) early termination charges quantifying the § 3.4 exposure, (ii) committed volumes or minimum purchase obligations, (iii) any hiring restriction (we would then negotiate to the mutual 12-month fallback limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire), and (iv) initial term length, given the § 3.2 renewal mechanic.
- If a Service Option Attachment or Order Form later introduces usage verification, apply the AUDIT parameters at that point.
- Raise a vendor-granted MFN as a commercial ask in negotiation (upside, not a deviation).
"}
